title: Castelli updates the Gabba and Perfetto with new Polartec AirCore fabric
content:
Cyclist
Castelli updates the Gabba and Perfetto with new Polartec AirCore fabric

The Castelli Gabba has had a makeover, with its fourth generation switching from Gore-Tex Infinium fabric to Polartec AirCore. Now called the Gabba Pro, it’s joined by the new long sleeved Perfetto 4 and Perfetto Pro in using Polartec’s new fabric. 

Castelli worked with Polartec to develop AirCore, which it claims is not only water-repellent and windproof, but also lightweight, highly breathable and PFAS-free. 

Launching the new Gabba Pro, Castelli global brand manager, Steve Smith said, ‘It’s always an exciting moment introducing a new Gabba into the range as it’s a jacket that revolutionised the cycling apparel market in the same way AirCore transformed how modern cyclists dress for colder conditions.’

The Castelli Gabba Pro uses 150gsm AirCore fabric, which Smith says is tuned for riding at higher speeds and intensity. It has a close-to-body fit and short sleeves and is designed to be worn with arm warmers when it’s cool. As well as the all-black option, there’s a Race Edition, which comes complete with pro-style logos on the upper chest.

Castelli says that the Gabba Pro weighs 196g in an unspecified size. It’s available in men’s fit only, in sizes XS to 3XL and is priced at £230 / $320 / €260. For the moment, it’s only available via Castelli’s website.

Update to the Castelli Perfetto and the new Perfetto Pro

Castelli launched the Perfetto RoS 3 last year, the first use of this AirCore fabric worldwide.

But Smith says that customer feedback on the Perfetto RoS 3 was that they wanted more warmth, so in response the Perfetto 4, designed for everyday riders, uses a more insulated 219gsm version of AirCore.

Castelli says the Perfetto 4 is tailored for temperatures between 40C and 120C, with light showers a possibility. The contrasting shoulder taping that was a feature of the older Perfetto and the Gabba RoS is transparent on the new jackets. 

It has eliminated the venting zips, as it claims that the new jacket’s breathability is adequate without. There’s an updated tail to fend off road spray and metal drainage holes have returned to the pockets – a feature of the original Gabba when it was launched in 2013.   

The Perfetto 4 is available in men’s sizes from XS to 3XL and four colours and women’s sizes from XS to XL and three colours. Castelli claims a weight of 286g for the men’s and 239g for the women’s jacket. 

It’s priced at £280 / $330 / €260.

As with the Gabba, the Perfetto 4 Pro uses the original 150gsm AirCore. It’s cut differently to the Perfetto 4 too, with a closer, sleeker fit. It is available in men’s fit only, sizes XS to 3XL and again in four colours. It’s claimed to weigh 226g and is priced at £300 / $350 / €280.   

‘All three jackets provide excellent warmth, breathability and protection against intermittent showers but if torrential rain is forecast, we’d recommend the Gabba R for complete waterproof coverage,’ says Smith.

The three jackets aren’t the only Castelli products to use AirCore, with a raft of other jackets launched last year using the product, including the suitably named AirCore One and the Alpha 150, which uses an AirCore outer layer with a Polartec Alpha insulating layer underneath. The fabric also finds its way into the Polare bib tights and even the Estremo 2 shoe covers.

AirCore is made from recycled polyester, with a very tight weave to repel water but retain high breathability, so that riders don’t get drenched with sweat in place of rain. Polartec claims water vapour permeability of 25,000 g/m²/24h and that AirCore will support a hydrostatic head of 5,000mm. Castelli and Sportful have exclusive use of the fabric for cycling garments.
